```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
```

This vignette walks through a small popPK analysis with **nmtools**, from the
data set and a first control stream to the comparison of two models. NONMEM is not needed to read it:
the package ships an example project whose NONMEM runs have already been
made. The chunks that call NONMEM are shown but not run.

```{r setup}
library(nmtools)
ex <- system.file("extdata", "example", package = "nmtools")
list.files(ex, recursive = TRUE)
```

The data are **simulated** (60 fictitious subjects, single oral dose of
100 mg, 9 samples each, body weight `WT` and a binary genotype `GENO`; see
`README.txt` and `sim_example_data.R` in the example folder). Two models were
fitted with NONMEM 7.6:

* `run1`: one-compartment model with first-order absorption, no covariate
  (BASE);
* `run2`: same model with weight on CL (estimated exponent) and V (exponent
  fixed to 1), and genotype on CL (FINAL).

## 1. The data set

`nm_read_csv()` reads a NONMEM data set, identifies the reserved columns and
computes the time after dose. `nm_summary()` gives a short diagnostic.

```{r data}
dat <- nm_read_csv(file.path(ex, "example_data.csv"))
nm_summary(dat$data)
```

```{r plot-dv}
nm_plot_dv(dat$data, scales = "log", verbose = FALSE)
```

## 2. Writing a control stream

`nm_write_ctl()` writes a first control stream from the columns of the data
set: here a one-compartment model with first-order absorption, as in
`run1`, with a combined error model. `$INPUT` follows the column order of
the file, the `#` of `#ID` becomes the `IGNORE` character, and the
covariates are written in a `cotab` table.

```{r write-ctl}
ctl <- nm_write_ctl(data = "../example_data.csv",
                    input = file.path(ex, "example_data.csv"),
                    error = "combined", theta_init = c(CL = 4, V = 40),
                    covariates = c("WT", "GENO"))
ctl
```

`nm_ctl_check()` looks for inconsistencies that can be seen without NM-TRAN,
such as a THETA, ETA or EPS used without a declaration. It also works on a
control stream written by hand:

```{r check-ctl}
nm_ctl_check(ctl)
nm_ctl_check(file.path(ex, "run1.ctl"))
```

Three functions transform a control stream: `nm_ctl_mu()` (MU referencing,
for the EM and Bayesian methods), `nm_ctl_iov()` (inter-occasion
variability) and `nm_ctl_m3()` (M3 method for data below the limit of
quantification). With `reference`, `nm_ctl_check()` shows what changed:

```{r mu-ctl}
mu <- nm_ctl_mu(ctl)
nm_ctl_check(mu, reference = ctl)
```

Use `file = "run3.ctl"` to write the result to disk.

## 3. Running NONMEM

`nm_run()` calls the `nmfe` launcher directly (no PsN, no Wings for NONMEM).
By default each run gets its own `<run>.reg` subdirectory, as in the example
folder; `run_subdir = ""` runs it next to its control stream instead. The
functions that write files are run here on a copy of the example folder.

```{r run, eval = FALSE}
file.copy(ex, tempdir(), recursive = TRUE)
proj <- file.path(tempdir(), "example")
log <- nm_run(
  nmfe_path       = "C:/nm76g64/run/nmfe76.bat",
  ctl_files       = c("run1.ctl", "run2.ctl"),
  analysis_dir    = proj,
  skip_terminated = FALSE
)
```

## 4. Results of all the runs

`nm_extract_runs()` reads every run of a folder: objective function,
minimisation and covariance status, parameters with their RSE and
shrinkage. Parameters are named from the model code (`CL`, `V`, `KA`...).

```{r runs}
runs <- nm_extract_runs(ex)
runs$runs[, c("run", "ofv", "dOFV", "min_ok", "cov_status")]
nm_compare_runs(runs, what = "value", format = TRUE)
```

The link between each THETA/ETA and the PK parameter comes from
`nm_identify_parameters()`:

```{r identify}
nm_identify_parameters(file.path(ex, "run2.ctl"))$parameter_table
```

A parameter table of one run can be exported to Word with
`nm_extract_run_table()` (packages flextable and officer):

```{r run-table, eval = FALSE}
nm_extract_run_table(run_rep = proj, run_name = "run2")
```

## 5. Goodness-of-fit plots

```{r gof, fig.height = 4}
gof <- nm_gof(file.path(ex, "run2.reg", "sdtab2"))
names(gof$plots)
gof$plots$dv_pred
gof$plots$cwres_time
```

## 6. Comparing two models

`nm_compare()` puts the BASE and FINAL runs side by side, subject by subject
and observation by observation.

```{r compare}
cmp <- nm_compare(file.path(ex, "run1.reg"), file.path(ex, "run2.reg"),
                  labels = c("BASE", "FINAL"))
cmp
```

## 7. Visual predictive check

The VPC needs two more NONMEM runs (the model re-run on the data, and the
simulations). `nm_vpc_ctl()` writes and launches them, then `nm_vpc()` draws
the VPC or the prediction-corrected VPC.

```{r vpc, eval = FALSE}
nm_vpc_ctl(run_name = "run2", analysis_dir = proj,
           nmfe_path = "C:/nm76g64/run/nmfe76.bat", n_sim = 500)
nm_vpc(run_name = "run2", analysis_dir = proj,
       col_names = c("NSIM", "ID", "TIME", "AMT", "MDV", "DV", "PRED", "IPRED"),
       type = 2)
```

## 8. Uncertainty

`nm_profile()` (likelihood profiles), `nm_bootstrap()` (case bootstrap) and
`nm_jackknife()` (influence of each subject) also run NONMEM and are not
executed here.

```{r uncertainty, eval = FALSE}
prof <- nm_profile("C:/nm76g64/run/nmfe76.bat", file.path(proj, "run2.ctl"),
                   param = "THETA(6)", from = 0.1, to = 1, by = 0.1)
boot <- nm_bootstrap(file.path(proj, "run2.ctl"), "C:/nm76g64/run/nmfe76.bat",
                     n = 500)
jk <- nm_jackknife(file.path(proj, "run2.reg", "run2.ctl"),
                   nmfe_path = "C:/nm76g64/run/nmfe76.bat")
plot(jk, "scatter")
```

The covariate assessment based on the Wasserstein distance is described in
`vignette("wasserstein", package = "nmtools")`.
